text:
The Senators got their goalie back at the right time. Linus Ullmark returned Thursday after missing nine games with a lower-body strain, made 26 saves, and Shane Pinto won it 4-3 in overtime against a Colorado team that lost Nathan MacKinnon and Cale Makar to injuries in the second period. Before he got hurt Ullmark was 7-1-0 with a .945 save percentage. Samuel Ersson held the fort unevenly in between.

At 12-6-2 and 26 points, Ottawa's record matches its play reasonably well. The Senators have 51% of the expected goals (the quality of chances for and against) and 53% at five-on-five, and our numbers have them about three points ahead of what they've earned. That still makes them a 78% bet for the playoffs.

The engine is on the back end. Thomas Chabot and Jordan Spence have outscored opponents 14-6 with 60% of the expected goals, while Jake Sanderson and Artem Zub, who played his 400th NHL game Thursday, break even. Up front, the Zetterlund, Cozens and Stützle trio has looked dangerous in a small sample; the Pinto and Amadio groups have spent too long in their own end.

Hits have followed this team: Hayden Hodgson served a two-game suspension for boarding, Dylan Cozens faced questions over his hit on Anaheim's AJ Greer, and Nick Cousins left Tuesday's game after a hit from Jakob Chychrun that officials reviewed and ruled clean. Ottawa draws more penalties than it takes (5.05 to 4.7 a game).
headline: Ullmark is back, and the Senators look sturdy
